aos-manual.title: Residential Gas Water Heater: Installation Instructions and Use & Care Guide (document 100400765)
quotes: Drain and flush tank, clean condensate pan, and remove and inspect anode rod after first six months of operation and at least annually thereafter.
Depending on the hardness of your water, repeat this process at least annually, or more frequently if needed.
Failure to drain and flush the water heater of sediment can deteriorate the tank and drain valve and cause leaks resulting in property damage.
Note that sediment in the bottom of the tank may clog the valve and prevent it from draining. If you cannot get the tank to drain, contact a qualified person.
Allow a hot water faucet to run full for at least three minutes to make sure the tank has all the air removed and is completely full of water.
It may take an hour or more for the tank of cold water to heat up.
If you use a water softener, your anode rod will deplete faster than normal.
Anode rods are a consumable item and are not covered under warranty.
A small amount of water dripping from the Temperature and Pressure (T&P) Relief Valve usually means the home's water pressure is too high and/or you need a Thermal Expansion Tank.
Install a Pressure Reducing Valve (PRV) on the main cold water supply line. Adjust the PRV to between 50 and 60 psi.
Do not cap or plug the T&P Relief Valve or discharge pipe, and do not operate the water heater without a functioning T&P Relief Valve; this could cause an explosion.
If the T&P Relief Valve is discharging large amounts of very hot water, turn the gas supply valve off and call a qualified person.

When a gas water heater is first lit and the tank is cold, condensation often forms inside the water heater... Condensation is not a leak and will go away once the tank reaches normal operating temperature.
If you have no hot water after two hours, refer to the Troubleshooting Section.
Plumbing Leak. Even a small leak in the hot water side of the home's plumbing system can make it appear that the water heater is producing little to no hot water.

Harmless bacteria normally present in tap water can multiply in water heaters and give off a 'rotten egg' smell... the standard anode rod ... can be replaced with a special zinc anode rod which may help reduce or eliminate the odor.
To protect the tank, an anode rod must be installed in the water heater at all times or the warranty is void.
WHAT TO DO IF YOU SMELL GAS: Do not try to light any appliance. Do not touch any electrical switch; do not use any phone in your building. Immediately call your gas supplier from a neighbor's phone.
The 'HOT' setting sets the water temperature to approximately 120°F, reducing the risk of scald injury.
Most codes allow a maximum incoming water pressure of 80 psi (we recommend a working pressure no higher than 50-60 psi).
Connect the water pressure gauge to an outside faucet and measure the maximum water pressure experienced throughout a 24-hour period (highest water pressures often occur at night).
Install a metal drain pan... Install an automatic leak detection... device.
Apply thread sealant tape or pipe joint compound and reinstall the anode rod tightly using a 1-1/16" socket wrench with an extension.

aos-leaking.title: What to do when your hot water heater is leaking
quotes: Wipe the area completely dry with towels, then watch for new moisture. If it reappears within a few hours, you have a leak.
Leaks typically develop at four points on your tank.
Tank water heaters hold 30-80 gallons, and a more serious leak can flood your home in a matter of hours.
Water pressure above 80 PSI can turn a small crack into a gushing leak.
Most residential tanks take 20-30 minutes to empty.
Water soaking into drywall, flooring, or insulation creates mold growth within 24-48 hours.
Electric Water Heater Leaks: Failed gaskets around heating elements cause water to seep from the side of the tank where elements penetrate through the steel.
Gas Water Heater Leaks: Moisture near the burner assembly or gas line connection requires immediate professional help since water can interfere with combustion and create carbon monoxide risks.

aos-leak-guide.title: Water heater leaking: causes, signs and fixes
quotes: The anode rod, or 'sacrificial' rod, corrodes over time to protect the tank from rusting. These rods usually last 3-5 years before they need to be replaced.
If the T&P valve is leaking due to high pressure, turning down the thermostat could stop the leak. The addition of a properly sized and charged expansion tank is the solution to this issue.
A water leak coming from the base of the heater is often the first indication of a serious problem.

aos-not-working.title: Water heater not working? Common problems and fixes
quotes: A very common reason for an electric water heater not working is a tripped circuit breaker.
Thermostat Issues: Causes temperature inconsistencies and can trip the high-limit safety switch (red reset button), often due to a grounded heating element or a faulty lower thermostat.
Gas Supply Problems: Prevents burner ignition and can also cause the pilot to extinguish.
Plan your showers around recovery time: gas tanks need 30-40 minutes, electric tanks need 60-90 minutes.
Electric Water Heaters: Turn off power at the circuit breaker before touching anything.
If you smell rotten eggs or suspect a gas leak for any reason, turn off the gas supply valve immediately and call a professional.
Check water pressure, which should be 50-60 PSI and no higher than 80 PSI, and install a thermal expansion tank.

Fix: Flush the water heater with a solution of water and hydrogen peroxide. For persistent issues, increase the water temperature to 140 degrees F for a short period to kill bacteria, then return to a safer temperature. Install mixing valves to prevent scalding. Alternatively, installing an aluminum/zinc composite anode rod can also help eliminate odor-causing bacteria.

aos-maintenance.title: Water heater maintenance (draining, flushing, anode rod, T&P valve)
quotes: Most types of tank water heaters require flushing at least once per year. If you live in a hard water area, you may need to flush your water heater more often.
Ideally, you should turn your water heater off for a few hours before draining the tank.
For an electric water heater, it is critical to make sure the tank is full before turning the power back on.
A rod in good working condition should be smooth and around a half inch in diameter. If the sacrificial anode rod shows signs of deterioration or has several inches of exposed core wire, replace it.
How long an anode rod will last depends on what chemicals are in the water, how much hot water is used, and whether or not a water softener is installed.
The T&P valve should be inspected once a year by the consumer and every 5 years by a professional.

aos-checklist.title: Water heater maintenance checklist
quotes: Have your hot water heater serviced once a year. If you have hard water in your area, get it serviced twice a year since mineral buildup happens faster.
Tankless models skip these tasks but need descaling, which means flushing out mineral deposits that build up inside the unit where water gets heated.
Once the rod's mostly gone or 6 inches of core wire is exposed, your tank starts rusting from the inside out.

ge-anode.title: Water heater: anode rod maintenance and service
quotes: The anode rod must be removed from the water heater's tank and inspected annually, and replaced when more than 6" (15.2 cm) of core wire is exposed at either end of the rod.
Please be aware that artificially-softened water will cause the anode rod to consume more rapidly.
Operation with the anode rod removed will shorten the life of the glass-lined tank and will void warranty coverage.
Some areas have water conditions that may cause an odor to develop in the water heater. Special alloy replacement rods are available to address the condition.
Failure to replace the anode rod when consumed voids the warranty for the tank.

rinnai-flush.title: 13-step tankless water heater flushing procedure
quotes: It's important to flush those mineral deposits at least once a year.
Use 4 gallons (15.1 liters) of undiluted white vinegar to clean your tankless water heater. Never use chemical solutions of any kind.
This procedure may take up to 45 minutes.

cpsc-scald.title: Avoiding Tap Water Scalds (Publication 5098)
quotes: The U.S. Consumer Product Safety Commission (CPSC) urges all users to lower their water heaters to 120 degrees Fahrenheit.
Most adults will suffer third-degree burns if exposed to 150 degree water for two seconds.

rheem-lifespan.title: Water heater lifespan: when to repair vs. replace (March 25, 2026)
quotes: Flush the tank annually; replace the anode rod every 3-4 years; aim for 40-60 psi.
If the leak is from the tank itself, replacement is usually required.

corro-protec.title: How a powered anode rod works
quotes: Unlike traditional rods, which sacrifice themselves, they use a small electrical current to prevent corrosion.
Diagram of a standard powered anode rod with power supply, indicator light.

rinnai-tb.title: Technical Bulletin TB-188: Sensei enhanced flush procedure
quotes: When unit has finished draining, remove the in-line filter at the cold water inlet and clean out any residue.
Clean filters immediately after flush is complete.

safety.gasSmell: If you smell gas, do not light anything, do not touch electrical switches or use a phone in the building, and call your gas supplier from a neighbor's phone.
safety.powerOff: On an electric water heater, turn the power off at the circuit breaker before you touch anything.

leakPoints.caption: Where a tank water heater leaks, what it usually means, and what fixes it

rows.where: Pipe connections on top of the tank
rows.cause: Loose or corroded fittings on the hot outlet or cold inlet

rows.where: Relief valve on the side or top, or its discharge pipe
rows.cause: Water pressure too high, thermal expansion, debris in the valve, or a failed valve
rows.fix: Check pressure, add an expansion tank, replace a failed valve (never plug it)

rows.cause: Valve not fully closed, worn washer, or a failed valve
rows.fix: Close it fully; replace the valve if it keeps dripping

rows.where: Side of an electric tank, at an element
rows.fix: Power off, drain, replace the gasket or element

rows.where: Around the burner of a gas tank
rows.cause: Condensation on a cold tank, or water reaching the burner from a leak above
rows.fix: Condensation clears as the tank heats; any other water near the burner needs a professional

rows.where: Tank bottom or a wet tank body
rows.fix: None: the tank cannot be repaired

flushSchedule.caption: How often to flush, by water heater type and water (manufacturer guidance)

rows.after: At least once a year, more often with hard water
rows.also: Inspect the anode rod; operate the relief valve per its label

rows.after: At least once a year, more often with hard water
rows.also: Inspect the anode rod; refill fully before power goes back on
Inspect the anode more often: softened water uses it up faster

rows.after: Descale at least once a year

noHotByType.caption: No hot water: the first things to check, by type

rows.first: The breaker in your panel (a very common cause)
rows.then: The red reset button (high-limit switch) behind the upper panel, with the power off
rows.pro: The breaker or reset trips again, or an element or thermostat has failed

rows.first: That the gas valve is open and the control knob is not on Off or Vacation
rows.then: Whether the pilot is lit; relight only by the label on the heater
rows.pro: The pilot will not stay lit, or you smell gas

rows.first: The status light on the gas control
rows.then: Its flash code in the manual; a lockout can clear after a wait
rows.pro: The code points to a sensor, igniter or venting fault

rows.first: The error code on the display, and that the gas or power is on
rows.then: Whether the inlet filter is blocked or scale is due to be flushed
rows.pro: The code repeats after a reset or names a part

rows.first: Other taps: if they are hot, the heater is fine
rows.then: That tap's mixing valve (common in shower controls)
rows.pro: The valve needs replacing and you are not comfortable doing it
